findings.issue_text: [High/bug] src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py — `organization_context` is referenced but never defined in the endpoint's `get()`, causing `NameError` when `optimized_pagination=true` is passed

[High/bug] src/sentry/api/paginator.py:~180 — Allowing negative `start_offset` when `cursor.is_prev` crashes with Django's `AssertionError` on negative slicing and has undefined pagination semantics; also changes behavior globally for all existing paginators

[High/security] src/sentry/api/paginator.py / organization_auditlogs.py — `OptimizedCursorPaginator` honors attacker-supplied negative cursor offsets behind a broken 'superuser or global access' check, enabling arbitrary-position dataset access and should be removed

[Critical/data] src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:~60-70 and src/sentry/spans/buffer.py — `zpopmin` silently evicts oldest spans from oversized segments after removing `max_segment_spans` check, flushing incomplete segments (possibly missing root span) as if complete, causing silent data corruption
[Medium/bug] src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua — Eviction happens with no metric or log when spans are dropped, making span loss unobservable; should emit a metric
[Medium/bug] src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/factory.py — `val["end_timestamp_precise"]` raises `KeyError` when the field is absent; should use `val.get()` with a safe default

[Medium/doc_defect] src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:30 — Redirect-loop cap reduced from 10000 to 1000 with the explanatory comment deleted rather than updated, leaving the trade-off undocumented

[Medium/api] src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py — `optimized_pagination` query param lets clients switch between paginators with incompatible cursors mid-pagination, producing corrupt results; behavior should be fixed server-side

[Medium/maintenance] src/sentry/api/paginator.py — `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result` duplicates `OffsetPaginator.get_result` (including a shared prev/offset bug comparing against unclamped offset) instead of subclassing or reusing logic
[Low/test_gap] tests/sentry/spans/test_buffer.py — No test covers the new >1000-span eviction path (zpopmin), removal of `max_segment_spans` skip, or that `zadd` scores are used for eviction ordering

[Low/data] src/sentry/spans/buffer.py (`process_spans`) — Switching `sadd` to `zadd` means duplicate re-processing overwrites scores, which combined with zpopmin eviction reorders which duplicate survives; worth confirming intended

goldens.comment: OptimizedCursorPaginator's negative-offset branch in get_result() passes cursor.offset directly as start_offset to queryset slicing when enable_advanced_features is True and cursor.offset < 0.
In BasePaginator.get_result(), when cursor.is_prev is True, it sets start_offset = offset without clamping, allowing negative offset values to be passed to queryset slicing.
OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key uses floor/ceil on a datetime key (order_by='-datetime'), causing TypeError.
Accessing .has_global_access on organization_context.member can raise an AttributeError when organization_context is None, particularly for non-superuser non-member users.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [High/bug] src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py — `organization_context` is referenced but never defined in the endpoint's `get()`, causing `NameError` when `optimized_pagination=true` is passed

adjudication.rationale: In `organization_auditlogs.py` the new code sets `enable_advanced = request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access`, but within the shown `get()` hunk there is no definition or assignment to `organization_context` before this use. If `optimized_pagination=true` is passed (and even just evaluating `enable_advanced`), this would raise a `NameError` unless `organization_context` is defined elsewhere in `get()` outside the displayed context.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [High/bug] src/sentry/api/paginator.py:~180 — Allowing negative `start_offset` when `cursor.is_prev` crashes with Django's `AssertionError` on negative slicing and has undefined pagination semantics; also changes behavior globally for all existing paginators
matched_golden_ids: OptimizedCursorPaginator's negative-offset branch in get_result() passes cursor.offset directly as start_offset to queryset slicing when enable_advanced_features is True and cursor.offset < 0.
In BasePaginator.get_result(), when cursor.is_prev is True, it sets start_offset = offset without clamping, allowing negative offset values to be passed to queryset slicing.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both comments identify that in OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result() a negative cursor offset can be used directly as the queryset slice start (i.e., a negative start_offset), leading to Django negative slicing/assertion issues and incorrect pagination semantics. The candidate frames it around cursor.is_prev, but it’s the same underlying bug: permitting negative start offsets in queryset slicing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [High/security] src/sentry/api/paginator.py / organization_auditlogs.py — `OptimizedCursorPaginator` honors attacker-supplied negative cursor offsets behind a broken 'superuser or global access' check, enabling arbitrary-position dataset access and should be removed

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly adds support for negative offsets: `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result` slices the Django queryset with `start_offset = cursor.offset` when `enable_advanced_features` and `cursor.offset < 0` (and the base paginator change also allows negative `offset` when `cursor.is_prev`). Django `QuerySet` slicing does not support negative indices and will raise, so an attacker/user supplying a cursor with a negative offset can trigger server errors (DoS) on these code paths. However, the finding’s claim about “arbitrary-position dataset access” and a “broken 'superuser or global access' check” isn’t verifiable from the diff; the check is present and negative slicing is more likely to error than grant extra access.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Critical/data] src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:~60-70 and src/sentry/spans/buffer.py — `zpopmin` silently evicts oldest spans from oversized segments after removing `max_segment_spans` check, flushing incomplete segments (possibly missing root span) as if complete, causing silent data corruption

adjudication.rationale:
The diff changes span buffering from Redis SETs to ZSETs and introduces a hard cap in `add-buffer.lua`:
- It computes `span_count` and if `span_count > 1000` it executes `redis.call("zpopmin", set_key, span_count - 1000)`, which silently discards entries (the lowest-scored/oldest by `end_timestamp_precise`) with no logging/metrics.
- In `buffer.py`, the prior protection that aborted processing when `len(payloads[key]) > self.max_segment_spans` is removed entirely, so oversized segments are no longer rejected; instead they will be truncated by the Lua script.
This is verifiable from the diff and constitutes real data loss/truncation behavior introduced by the PR (and it also hardcodes `1000` rather than using `self.max_segment_spans`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua — Eviction happens with no metric or log when spans are dropped, making span loss unobservable; should emit a metric

adjudication.rationale:
The diff adds a hard cap in `src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua`:

```lua
if span_count > 1000 then
    redis.call("zpopmin", set_key, span_count - 1000)
end
```

This will drop spans from the buffer when the sorted set exceeds 1000 entries, and the script does not emit any metric/log when this eviction happens. That makes span loss due to this new eviction behavior unobservable. It’s a concrete, diff-introduced observability gap, but not a strictly verifiable correctness defect by itself (it may be an intended tradeoff).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/factory.py — `val["end_timestamp_precise"]` raises `KeyError` when the field is absent; should use `val.get()` with a safe default

adjudication.rationale: In `process_batch` the diff adds `end_timestamp_precise=val["end_timestamp_precise"]` (dict subscript) with no fallback. This will indeed raise `KeyError` if a consumed span message lacks that field (e.g., older/alternate producers), but the diff itself doesn’t prove such messages can occur since tests and the imported `SpanEvent` schema now include it.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/doc_defect] src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:30 — Redirect-loop cap reduced from 10000 to 1000 with the explanatory comment deleted rather than updated, leaving the trade-off undocumented

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `for i = 0, 10000 do  -- theoretically this limit means that segment trees of depth 10k may not be joined together correctly.` changed to `for i = 0, 1000 do` with the explanatory inline comment removed (not updated). That leaves the rationale/trade-off for the reduced redirect-loop cap undocumented, but this is not itself a verifiable functional defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/api] src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py — `optimized_pagination` query param lets clients switch between paginators with incompatible cursors mid-pagination, producing corrupt results; behavior should be fixed server-side

adjudication.rationale: The endpoint now conditionally selects `paginator_cls=OptimizedCursorPaginator` vs `DateTimePaginator` based on the client-controlled `optimized_pagination` query param (and an auth gate). There is no server-side coupling between the cursor in the request and the paginator that generated it; a client can send a cursor obtained from one mode while requesting the other mode, leading to the cursor being interpreted under different semantics. Since these are different paginator implementations (and likely different cursor/value expectations), this can produce incorrect/"corrupt" pagination behavior. This switching behavior is introduced directly by the new branching in `organization_auditlogs.py`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/maintenance] src/sentry/api/paginator.py — `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result` duplicates `OffsetPaginator.get_result` (including a shared prev/offset bug comparing against unclamped offset) instead of subclassing or reusing logic

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result` that largely reimplements the same pagination flow already present in existing paginator `get_result` logic (cursor defaulting, limit clamping, build_queryset, hits handling, offset/extra computation, prev trimming, reverse, build_cursor, post_query_filter). This is a real maintenance/architecture concern introduced by the change (duplication instead of factoring/reuse). However, the finding’s specific claim about a “shared prev/offset bug comparing against unclamped offset” isn’t clearly verifiable from the shown code, since the `len(results) == offset + limit + extra` comparison is only reached in the `cursor.is_prev` branch where `start_offset` equals `offset` unless the new negative-offset path is used.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/test_gap] tests/sentry/spans/test_buffer.py — No test covers the new >1000-span eviction path (zpopmin), removal of `max_segment_spans` skip, or that `zadd` scores are used for eviction ordering

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new nontrivial behavior in the Redis Lua script `add-buffer.lua`: it switches from sets to sorted sets (`zunionstore`/`zcard`) and adds an eviction branch `if span_count > 1000 then redis.call("zpopmin", set_key, span_count - 1000) end`, which implies ordering by ZSET score (now populated via `SpansBuffer.process_spans` using `zadd(... {span.payload: span.end_timestamp_precise})`). In `spans/buffer.py`, the previous `max_segment_spans` skip logic during `_load_segment_data` is removed (the whole block checking `len(payloads[key]) > self.max_segment_spans` is deleted). The shown test changes in `tests/sentry/spans/test_buffer.py` (and others) only add `end_timestamp_precise` fields but do not add coverage/assertions for the new >1000 eviction behavior, score-based ordering effects, or the removed `max_segment_spans` skip path. This is a concrete test-gap issue tied to the new/changed logic, not a directly verifiable runtime defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/data] src/sentry/spans/buffer.py (`process_spans`) — Switching `sadd` to `zadd` means duplicate re-processing overwrites scores, which combined with zpopmin eviction reorders which duplicate survives; worth confirming intended

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes span buffering from Redis sets to sorted sets: `process_spans` now does `p.zadd(set_key, {span.payload: span.end_timestamp_precise ...})` (src/sentry/spans/buffer.py), and the Lua script later enforces a cap via `zpopmin` after computing `span_count` (src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua). With ZSET semantics, re-adding the same `span.payload` will update/overwrite its score, which can change its ordering relative to eviction (`zpopmin` removes lowest-score members). That doesn’t prove incorrectness, but it’s a real behavioral change worth confirming is intended (e.g., whether duplicates should refresh timestamps and thus survive eviction).
